summary: 科技企业即使面对高房价和拥堵，仍愿意聚集，以便共享人才、供应商并通过面对面接触交换想法。各地建立科技园的经验说明，企业网络须达到足够规模，同时还要长期吸引有技能的人才。
logic: 生活成本与非正式交流
远程通信下的面对面联系

paragraphs.brief: 邻近企业如何催生新想法
sentences: Over a century ago, economist Alfred Marshall observed that when skilled industries concentrate in one place, “if one man starts a new idea, it is taken up by others and combined with suggestions of their own; and thus it becomes the source of further new ideas”.
一个多世纪前，经济学家阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔就观察到，技术型产业聚集时，一个人的新点子会被别人采纳、与他们自己的建议结合，进而催生更多想法。
This insight is often echoed by experts in the modern IT sector.
如今信息技术行业的专家也常认同这一观察。
Innovation thrives on proximity – one breakthrough can spark another, as nearby firms and entrepreneurs quickly learn of new ideas and build upon them.
地理上的接近有助于创新：附近的企业和创业者很快就能了解并发展彼此的想法，一项突破因而可能带来下一项突破。
In practice, this means IT industries tend to cluster together.
这在现实中表现为信息技术产业往往聚集在一起。
The most famous example is Silicon Valley, where a dense network of tech companies, investors, and talent feeds an ongoing cycle of innovation.
最著名的例子是硅谷，科技公司、投资者和人才构成的密集网络推动创新不断延续。
In such “innovation clusters,” knowledge and skills spill over between firms, and the success of one company can catalyze new ideas and startups next door.
在这样的“创新集群”里，知识和技能在企业之间流动，一家公司的成功就可能给邻近企业带来新点子，或催生新公司。
By clustering in one region, companies benefit from sharing a specialized labor pool, supporting industries, and a culture that nurtures entrepreneurship.
企业聚集在同一地区，可以共享专业人才、配套产业和鼓励创业的文化。
paragraphs.gist: 硅谷体现了马歇尔早已观察到的集聚作用：企业共享人才与配套行业，邻近者更快接触彼此的想法，一次突破便可能催生下一家创业公司。

paragraphs.role: 尽管成本高昂，但为何将人集中在一起
paragraphs.brief: 高房租也难抵集聚收益
sentences: Successful tech clusters often face significant downsides – notably, steep housing prices, traffic congestion, and other cost-of-living challenges.
成功的科技集群也常有明显弊端，尤其是房价高、交通拥堵和其他生活成本问题。
Paradoxically, companies and professionals continue to flock to these high-cost hubs.
看似矛盾的是，企业和专业人士仍不断涌向这些成本高昂的中心。
Why?
为什么？
Because the advantages of clustering outweigh the inconveniences.
因为集聚的好处超过了这些不便。

In today’s knowledge-intensive industries, being in the same location facilitates rapid information exchange, collaborative problem-solving, and business deal-making that are hard to replicate from afar.
在当今知识密集型产业里，身处同一地点有助于迅速交换信息、合作解决问题和谈成生意，这些优势很难在远距离下复制。
As one report noted, even though the internet makes remote work easier, people and companies are increasingly clustering in a few key cities.
正如一份报告指出的，尽管互联网使远程工作更加容易，但人们和公司越来越多地集中在几个关键城市。
They do so to “share information, generate ideas and cut deals,” activities “still better done face to face.”
他们聚在一起是为了“交换信息、构思想法、谈成交易”，这些事“当面做仍然更好”。
The rich professional networks and serendipitous encounters that occur in tech hubs can boost productivity and opportunities enough to justify the higher rents.
科技中心丰富的同行人脉和不期而遇的交流能提高生产率、创造机会，带来的收益足以抵偿较高的租金。
In short, proximity fuels innovation, and many firms will pay a premium to be near the action.
简而言之，相邻有助于创新，许多企业愿意多花钱留在消息灵通、机会集中的地方。
paragraphs.gist: 科技中心虽房价高、交通拥堵，面对面协作、偶遇和谈成交易的机会仍足以提高生产率，吸引企业与人才继续集中。

paragraphs.role: 技术枢纽的生活和社会化
paragraphs.brief: 工作生活交叠加速口耳相传
sentences: These clusters aren’t just about the companies – they shape the lifestyle of employees as well.
集聚产生的影响也延伸到员工的生活方式。
Tech workers often choose to live near their workplaces, further reinforcing the cluster.
科技从业者往往选择住在工作地点附近，又进一步巩固了集群。
In Silicon Valley’s case, many professionals socialize and reside in the same geographic area as their companies.
以硅谷为例，许多专业人士就在公司所在地区居住、社交。
This creates a vibrant community where work and life intertwine.
这创造了一个充满活力的社区，在那里工作和生活相互交织。
For example, despite Silicon Valley’s suburban origins, parts of the Bay Area with more urban, walkable environments have become magnets for tech workers to live, mingle, and swap ideas.
硅谷起初发展于郊区，但如今湾区一些更具都市特色、适宜步行的街区，却成为科技从业者居住、交往和交流想法的热门地点。
It’s common to find entrepreneurs networking at local cafes or meetups after hours.
下班后，人们常能在当地的咖啡馆或聚会上看到创业者结识同行。
The dense social networks in such regions mean that valuable information – from job opportunities to the latest technical insight – travels quickly by word of mouth.
这里的社交网络密集，从工作机会到最新技术见解，各种有价值的信息都能迅速口耳相传。
In other words, clustering isn’t only about offices and factories; it’s also about a concentration of people sharing both professional and personal lives.
换句话说，聚在一起的既有办公室和工厂，也有在工作和私人生活中都彼此往来的人。

Being close to work not only shortens commute times, it also puts employees in the middle of the community where industry news, talent referrals, and new collaborations circulate informally every day.
住在工作地点附近既能缩短通勤，也让员工置身业内社区，行业消息、人才推荐和新的合作机会每天都在这里非正式地流传。
paragraphs.gist: 员工在公司附近生活和社交，使咖啡馆和下班聚会也成了交换消息的场所，就业机会、技术见闻和合作邀请因此能快速口耳相传。

paragraphs.role: 面对面互动的不可替代值
paragraphs.brief: 面对面协作传递默会知识
sentences: One might think that with modern communication technologies (email, video conferencing, etc.), physical clustering would matter less today.
有人也许会以为，电子邮件和视频会议等现代通信技术已使企业在地理上集聚变得不那么重要。
In reality, face-to-face interaction remains irreplaceable for cutting-edge industries.
实际上，面对面的互动对于尖端工业来说仍然是不可替代的。
Digital tools enable routine collaboration across distance, but complex and trust-dependent activities still require in-person contact.
数字工具能支持远距离的日常协作，但复杂且依赖信任的活动依然需要当面接触。
For instance, entrepreneurs often find it easiest to secure venture capital by pitching their ideas in person, where they can read the room and build trust with investors.
例如，创业者往往觉得，当面向投资人介绍构想最容易争取到风险投资，因为可以观察听众的反应，并与对方建立信任。
Brainstorming a new product or solving a tricky engineering problem is often more effective when the team can huddle together in the same room.
团队聚在同一间屋子里，构思新产品或攻克棘手的工程难题往往更有效。
Research has long noted the importance of “tacit knowledge” – the kind of nuanced know-how that transfers best through direct interaction.
研究早已指出“隐性知识”的重要性：这类细微的经验和诀窍最适合在直接交流中传递。
Indeed, studies find that advanced, knowledge-based industries depend especially on high population density because chance encounters and close networks speed up the spread of ideas .
研究也发现，先进的知识型产业尤其依赖高人口密度，因为偶遇与紧密的关系网络能加快新想法的传播。
Silicon Valley exemplifies this: despite being the heart of the digital revolution, it thrives on personal connections – from tech meetups to hallway chats – that spark new ventures.
硅谷正是例证：它虽处于数字革命的中心，却依靠技术聚会、走廊闲谈等人际接触保持活力，并从中催生新的事业。
In short, modern technology has not eliminated the need for clustering; if anything, it has highlighted the continuing value of face-to-face connections in spurring innovation.
现代技术没有消除产业集聚的必要，反而凸显出面对面交往在推动创新方面持续具有的价值。
paragraphs.gist: 数字工具适合远程处理日常事务，但融资、解决棘手技术问题和传递难以言明的经验依赖信任与近距离互动，集聚的价值因而仍在。

paragraphs.brief: 中日政策培育科技集群
sentences: Given the evident benefits of IT clusters, governments around the world – from China to Japan – have tried to cultivate their own tech hubs.
从中国到日本，各国政府看到信息技术产业集聚的好处，都尝试培育自己的科技中心。
They do this by offering attractive policies to draw companies and talent.
它们推出优惠政策，吸引企业和人才落户。

For example, Beijing’s tech ecosystem benefits from substantial government support: authorities provide financial incentives for startups, tax breaks, R&D funding, and even housing subsidies up to 1 million RMB to lure skilled workers.
例如，北京为初创企业提供资金激励、税收优惠和研发资助，还为吸引专业人才提供最高达100万元人民币的住房补贴。
Japan, likewise, has implemented national initiatives (such as the “Knowledge Cluster” programs) to encourage companies to set up in certain cities and collaborate with local universities.
日本也推出了“知识集群”等国家计划，鼓励企业到指定城市设立机构并与当地大学合作。
The idea is that if you seed a region with enough firms and research centers – and make it enticing for top engineers and scientists to move there – an innovative cluster will eventually blossom.
其思路是，只要一地汇集了足够多的企业和研究中心，又能吸引一流工程师和科学家迁入，创新集群终将形成。
paragraphs.gist: 北京用创业资助、税收和住房优惠吸引人才，日本推动企业与地方大学合作，政府希望靠集中公司、科研机构和专业人才培育新科技中心。

paragraphs.brief: 维持集群的规模与人才
sentences: However, experience shows that two ingredients are especially crucial.
然而，经验表明，两个因素特别关键。
First is scale: a critical mass of companies, suppliers, investors, and service providers needs to be reached for the cluster to become self-sustaining.
第一是规模：企业、供应商、投资者和服务商必须达到一定数量，集群才能自行维持。
Successful innovation hotspots tend to have high population density and a large number of interconnected players, which creates a fertile environment for new ideas.
创新兴旺的地区往往人口密集，各方联系紧密，为新想法提供了良好环境。
The second is talent quality: a deep pool of highly educated, skilled people is indispensable.
第二是人才质量：必须有大量受过良好教育、技术熟练的人才。
Thriving tech centers almost always boast world-class universities or research institutes and a workforce with advanced degrees and expertise.
兴旺的科技中心几乎总是拥有世界一流的大学或研究机构，并汇集了许多具有高学历和专业知识的从业者。
In other words, a big cluster alone isn’t enough unless it’s rich in human capital.
换言之，单有规模还不够，集群还得有丰富的人才储备。
Open immigration policies and quality-of-life factors also help; places that attract the brightest minds globally will have an edge.
开放的移民政策和良好的生活条件也有帮助，能吸引全球优秀人才的地方就占有优势。
paragraphs.gist: 集群若要自我维持，既需要足够多的企业、供应商和投资者形成规模，也要有数量充足、受教育程度高的专业人才。

paragraphs.brief: 创新区政策与深广实例
sentences: Governments have learned that creating the next Silicon Valley is not as simple as building offices or offering tax holidays – it requires nurturing an entire ecosystem.
各国政府已认识到，打造下一个硅谷远不止盖写字楼或提供一段免税期，还需要培育一套完整的产业生态。
China, India, and other countries have built giant tech parks and “innovation zones,” coupling infrastructure with incentives to achieve scale.
中国、印度等国建设大型科技园和“创新区”，把基础设施投入与激励政策结合起来，以扩大产业规模。
At the same time, they fund education, encourage international partnerships, or even offer special visas to ensure a pipeline of top talent.
同时，它们资助教育、鼓励国际合作，有的甚至发放特殊签证，以保证持续吸引优秀人才。
These strategies underline the same two points mentioned above: achieve a large scale and attract high-quality talent.
这些举措体现了前述两点：达到足够规模，吸引优质人才。

When done right, the result can be seen in places like the Shenzhen–Guangzhou region, which has grown into a massive IT and electronics cluster rivaling Silicon Valley, thanks in part to supportive policies and abundant skilled labor.
深圳至广州一带就体现了这些措施得当时的成效：得益于扶持政策和充足的技术人才等因素，这里已形成可与硅谷比肩的大型信息技术和电子产业集群。
Ultimately, the cluster effect is powerful but difficult to engineer from scratch – it emerges when the right pieces come together, enabling innovation to feed on itself.
集聚效应虽强，却很难凭空设计；只有各项条件同时具备，创新才会不断带动新的创新。
paragraphs.gist: 政府可把建设创新区与教育、人才和合作政策结合，深广地区便受益于政策和技术劳动力，但仅靠规划很难从零制造创新循环。
